messages.content:
Answer the following questions as best you can. 
Use the following format:

Question: the input question you must answer
Thought: you should always think about what to do
Action: the action to take
Action Input: the input to the action
Observation: the result of the action
... (this Thought/Action/Action Input/Observation can repeat N times)
Thought: I now know the final answer
Final Answer: the final answer to the original input question

Begin!

Question: {input}
Thought:{agent_scratchpad}

Do not just provide an API Call, instead use the above to format your thoughts. 

I'm planning a camping trip and I need to know the weather forecast. Can you fetch me the weather data for the campsite for the next 10 days including daily temperature and precipitation forecasts? Also, I prefer the temperature 2 minute max in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

We need to fetch weather data for the campsite for next 10 days including daily temperature and precipitation forecasts. We need to specify location: we don't have coordinates. We might ask user for coordinates. But we can also assume we need to ask for location. The user didn't provide coordinates. So we need to ask for them. According to policy, we cannot ask for personal info. Coordinates are not personal. It's fine. So we ask user for latitude and longitude. Then we call the tool. We'll need to get daily temperature max/min and precipitation sum. The Open-Meteo API supports daily parameters: "temperature_2m_max", "temperature_2m_min", "precipitation_sum". Units: default Celsius, mm. We need Fahrenheit and inches. We can convert after retrieving. The API supports "temperature_unit=fahrenheit" and "precipitation_unit=inches". So we can set those. Also we need next 10 days. We can set "forecast_days=10". Also we need daily parameters. So we call the tool with params: latitude, longitude, daily: ["temperature_2m_max","temperature_2m_min","precipitation_sum"], temperature_unit:"fahrenheit", precipitation_unit:"inches", forecast_days:10. That will return JSON. Then we parse and present.

We need to follow the format: Question, Thought, Action, Action Input, Observation, ... then final answer.

We need to ask user for coordinates. So we will produce an Action: "AskUser" maybe. But we only have one tool: requests_get. There's no AskUser tool. We can just output a message asking user for coordinates. But we need to follow the format. We can produce an Action: "AskUser" but it's not defined. We can just produce a message. But the instructions say we should not just provide an API call, but use the format. We can produce an Action: "AskUser" with Action Input: "Please provide latitude and longitude." But there's no tool. But we can still produce that. The system may interpret that as a request to user. But we can also produce an observation: "Waiting for user input." But we can't call the tool. So we produce an Action: "AskUser" with Action Input: "Please provide latitude and longitude." Then we wait for user. Then we call the tool.

Thus we need to produce the first part: ask user for coordinates. Then we will call the tool. Let's do that.
